title: JavaScript ES6+ Core Check
description: Check your understanding of arrow functions, template literals, destructuring, spread, rest, enhanced object literals, Map, Set, and modern operators.
author: DailyCoder

questions.explanation: ES6 is also called ES2015 and was a major update to the JavaScript language standard.

questions.prompt: Which arrow function correctly returns the sum of `a` and `b`?
questions.explanation: Arrow functions use the `=>` syntax. A single expression can be returned implicitly.

questions.prompt: What is required when an arrow function with a block body should return a value?
questions.explanation: When an arrow function uses braces, it needs an explicit `return` to return a value.

questions.prompt: Which syntax correctly interpolates `name` into a string?
questions.explanation: Template literal interpolation requires backticks and `${}` placeholders.
Array destructuring is positional. The empty comma skips the second item.

questions.prompt: Which destructuring syntax renames the `name` property to `userName`?
questions.explanation: In object destructuring, `name: userName` reads the `name` property into a variable named `userName`.

questions.prompt: What does spread syntax do in `[0, ...numbers, 4]`?

options.text: Expands the elements of `numbers` into the new array

questions.explanation: Spread expands array elements into another array literal.

questions.prompt: What does rest syntax do in `function sum(...numbers)`?

options.text: Expands an array into separate arguments
Collects remaining arguments into an array
Stops the function from receiving arguments

questions.explanation: A rest parameter collects arguments into a real array.
When the variable name and property name match, property shorthand lets you write `{ name }`.

questions.prompt: Which data structure stores unique values?
questions.explanation: `Set` stores unique values and ignores duplicate entries.

questions.prompt: Which method reads a value from a `Map` by key?
questions.explanation: `Map.prototype.get()` reads the value associated with a key.

questions.prompt: What does nullish coalescing `??` check for?
questions.explanation: `??` uses the fallback only when the left side is `null` or `undefined`.
